data.gender_notes: Thomasine is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Thomas, meaning 'twin'. In Christian tradition, Thomasine may symbolize faith and loyalty, as Thomas was one of the twelve apostles who doubted the resurrection of Jesus but later professed his belief. The name Thomasine carries the meaning “Twin, companion” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Thomasine usually hope their child will grow to embody twin, companion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Thomasine belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Twin, companion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Thomasine total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
data.cultural_impact: The name Thomasine is primarily of European origin, and its presence in Christianity signifies the influence of the early Church and its traditions on European naming practices.
data.spiritual_significance: Thomasine is a name rooted in faith, as it is derived from Thomas, one of the twelve apostles. In the New Testament, Thomas is known as Doubting Thomas because he doubted the resurrection of Jesus Christ until he saw and touched the wounds in Jesus' hands and side. This narrative encourages perseverance, as Thomas ultimately professed his belief in the resurrected Christ. The name Thomasine can serve as a reminder for individuals to keep faith in difficult times and steadfast in their convictions.
